<reason>B accepted A’s strongest mechanism—the growing distance between teenagers and legal suppliers—while challenging whether that benefit justified lifelong exclusion. A established plausible additional deterrence, but overstated its implications for smoking prevalence and repeatedly dismissed unresolved resale and dependence burdens. B answered the pressure questions directly and made the comparison more concrete: prevention can help without establishing that permanent prohibition is proportionate.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal challenged the grandfathering rationale: protecting older smokers from withdrawal while denying legal access to younger, already-dependent adults leaves a substantive asymmetry. A’s appeals to administrative simplicity, cessation support, and “temporary unevenness” did not adequately resolve that lifelong burden.</best_rebuttal>
